display.title: The Purim Mitzvah Chart: Megillah, Graggers, Mishloach Manos and the Seudah
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi goes through the mitzvos of Purim, how to use a gragger properly, and why inviting a friend for Purim is just what Mordechai did.
display.summary_long: A short Purim talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi presents the Tzivos Hashem Purim mitzvah chart. First, hearing the Megillah at night and again in the morning: find out the times in your shul, and wait for the signal before using your gragger at Haman's name, because missing even one word means the mitzvah is not complete. Next comes mishloach manos, at least two ready-to-eat foods for a friend; matanos la'evyonim, tzedakah for the poor, given by hand or into a pushka; and a festive Purim seudah. Since what is good for you is good for your friend, every soldier in Hashem's army should invite a friend who knows little about Purim and teach them about it. That is just what Mordechai did when he gathered over 22,000 Jewish children to learn Torah, which brought the Purim salvation, and it helps bring Moshiach. The clip mentions that the Megillah reading that year began on Motzei Shabbos.
display.lesson: Do every mitzvah of Purim carefully and joyfully, and share Purim with a friend who doesn't know about it.

date.note: Megillah read 'this coming Shabbos night' after 13 Adar; Purim 5750 was Sunday 11 March 1990.

relations.note: Episode 419 (filename number); clip = 67-459 s of the episode.

quality.notes: Megillah timing (Motzei Shabbos) applies to Purim 5750 only.
